rounds.text: RBZ Jewellers Ltd is trading at a compelling valuation of 12.5x P/E [E1] and 12.29x against a sector benchmark of 28.18x [E6], while delivering outstanding financial returns with an ROE of 20.1% [E13] and an ROCE of 22.0% [E12]. The business demonstrates robust fundamental momentum, supported by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 43% [E14] and a 54% jump in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E19]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation models highlight a staggering margin of safety of 69.4% [E40], and the reverse DCF implies that today’s market price requires a mere 1.7% earnings growth [E41], sharply contrasting with the company's proven historical performance and a rules-based screen score of 89 out of 100 [E56]. Growth catalysts are firmly in place as management executes an aggressive retail expansion plan, launching the Surat store in Quarter 2 alongside Rajkot, Maninagar, and Gandhinagar stores in Quarter 3 [E75], while systematically scaling its higher-margin B2C mix toward a 50-50 target [E69]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -7 Cr for March 2026 [E29] and borrowings climbed to Rs 170 Cr [E33] as the company finances its ongoing capital expenditure build-up.

Despite reported revenue growth, RBZ Jewellers carries severe fundamental and structural risks, beginning with an alarming collapse in cash generation where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -7 Cr and free cash flow plummeted to Rs -40 Cr in March 2026 [E29, E30]. This translates to a dismal cash conversion ratio of -0.13x against reported profit, with operating cash flow representing a mere 13% of operating profit [E28, E31]. Compounding this liquidity strain, total borrowings nearly doubled from Rs 91 Cr to Rs 170 Cr within a single year [E33], while capital work-in-progress surged by 733.3% to Rs 25 Cr as aggressive retail expansion gets underway [E34]. Furthermore, operating margins are showing clear signs of compression, dropping two percentage points to 15% in June 2026 compared to the same quarter last year alongside an inconsistent margin trend [E25, E27]. Institutional confidence has completely evaporated, evidenced by foreign and domestic institutional holdings collapsing down to 0.03% and 0.01% respectively, generating an active institutional outflow signal [E36, E37, E38, E62]. Conceded: the company displays strong historical compounded sales and profit growth alongside high return metrics like an ROCE of 18.74% [E10, E14, E17]. Finally, the equity completely lacks dividend returns at 0.00% yield [E4, E55], leaving shareholders exposed to high annualised volatility of 62.4% and a brutal historical drawdown of -57.4% [E47, E48].

While the bear highlights negative cash flow [E28, E29, E30] and debt rising to Rs 170 Cr [E33], this reflects active capital deployment into inventory and expansion, evidenced by CWIP surging 733.3% [E34] to open four new stores in Surat, Rajkot, Maninagar, and Gandhinagar [E75, E90] with store capex break-even expected within a year [E92] and debt-to-equity controlled at 0.57x [E32, E71]. Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -7 Cr [E29], free cash flow stood at Rs -40 Cr [E30], institutional ownership declined [E36, E37, E38], and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E55]. However, retaining cash to fund high-return retail growth is superior for shareholders when the business delivers an ROCE of 18.74% to 22.0% [E10, E12] and an ROE of 18.28% to 20.1% [E9, E13]—more than double sector benchmarks [E9, E10]—backed by unutilized sanctioned debt facilities [E85] and solid 75.00% promoter ownership [E35]. The bear's focus on quarterly margin compression [E25, E27] ignores seasonal post-Akshay Tritiya buying lulls [E89], stagnant gold prices offering negligible inventory gains [E79], and lease accounting adjustments [E80], whereas TTM operating margins expanded by 2 percentage points [E24], EBITDA grew 39% YoY [E78], and sales surged 60% YoY [E57, E74]. Growth visibility remains robust as current factory utilization is only 50% [E81], corporate product mix expands into 18-karat jewellery [E70, E91], and long-term retail mix targets reach 75% [E69]. Trading at a discounted 12.29x P/E versus the sector benchmark of 28.18x [E6], alongside 54% TTM profit growth [E19] and a 100 relative strength rating [E45], the stock is severely under-appreciated relative to its DCF intrinsic value of Rs 585 per share [E39], which offers a massive 69.4% margin of safety [E40].

Conceded: the company delivers high profitability metrics like an ROE of 18.28% to 20.1% [E9, E13] and TTM sales surged 60% YoY [E57, E74]. However, the bull's framing of negative cash flows as mere active capital deployment [E28, E29, E30] masks a severe deterioration, where operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 7 Cr and free cash flow plunged to negative Rs 40 Cr [E29, E30]. While the bull dismisses institutional outflow by pointing to stable promoter holdings [E35], it ignores that foreign and domestic institutional investors have fled significantly, with foreign holdings dropping from 4.33% to 0.03% and domestic institutions falling from 3.03% to 0.01% [E36, E37]. The bull's defense of quarterly margin compression as a seasonal lul [E25, E27, E89] glosses over the concrete risk that carrying unhedged open inventory positions exposes the business directly to commodity price volatility [E87]. Furthermore, boasting about unutilized debt facilities of Rs 300 Cr [E85] ignores that actual borrowings already escalated sharply from Rs 91 Cr to Rs 170 Cr in a single year [E33]. Finally, the zero dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E55] combined with negative cash generation [E28, E29, E30] means shareholders bear all the cash burn risk without any cash return.

Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -7 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -40 Cr in Mar 2026 [E28, E29, E30]. While institutional holdings decreased [E36, E37], this exodus contrasts with rock-solid promoter commitment holding steady at 75.00% [E35]. The bear frames inventory risk around unhedged positions [E87], but management is actively transitioning financing toward Gold Metal Loans to properly keep inventory hedged [E86]. Although borrowings increased to Rs 170 Cr [E33], this capital is backing a massive +733.3% surge in capital-work-in-progress [E34] and fully funded retail expansions like the Surat store [E76], supported by substantial unutilized debt facilities of around Rs 300 Cr [E85]. Finally, the absence of dividends [E4, E55] is standard for an aggressive growth phase characterized by a stellar 60% YoY revenue jump [E57, E74], a robust 14.9% EBITDA margin [E78], and strong profit expansion [E19].

Conceded: the company maintains a stable promoter holding of 75.00% [E35]. However, the bull's dismissal of cash burn is dangerous, as negative operating cash flow of Rs -7 Cr and a free cash flow deficit of Rs -40 Cr in Mar 2026 expose a severe disconnect between reported profits and actual cash realization [E28, E29, E30]. Furthermore, citing future Gold Metal Loans to solve inventory risk ignores the company's explicit admission that carrying unhedged open positions directly threatens ongoing operations [E86, E87]. The bull normalizes rising borrowings reaching Rs 170 Cr and massive CWIP growth of +733.3% as mere growth spending, yet institutional investors have fled completely, slashing foreign and domestic holdings down to near-zero levels of 0.03% and 0.01% respectively [E33, E34, E36, E37, E62]. Finally, writing off the 0.00% dividend yield as standard growth procedure ignores the negative sentiment of zero shareholder payouts amid decelerating earnings growth and inconsistent quarterly margins [E4, E25, E27, E55, E61].

evidence.quote: For revenue mix, we see that job work percentage right now in Quarter 1 stands at 54% and, the mix has to, I think the B2B to B2C mix has to be 50-50 or so in a year or two and in long term it will be 75-25, 75 being retail.

evidence.fact: The company expects 18-karat jewellery to represent at least 20% of its corporate sales mix by the end of the year.
evidence.quote: So we have introduced this since December, our sales mix in corporate, before it was 100% 22 carat, I see by the end of this year, it will be at least 20% will be of 18 caratage.

evidence.fact: Management expects its debt-to-equity ratio to remain below 1:1 by the end of the current financial year.
evidence.quote: By the end of this financial year, we will be still below 1:1 ratio. I guess 0.8 will be debt and 1 equity.

evidence.fact: Management noted good demand in July, steady trends in August, and positive reception at IIJS.
evidence.quote: So July has been good. August so far has been right. IIJS has gone good, but still we would not want to really comment on numbers.

evidence.fact: Demand outlook for Quarter 2 appears promising as the company enters the period.
evidence.quote: And the demand side looks to be good and promising for Quarter 2, as we are approaching.

evidence.fact: Revenue increased by approximately 60% year-on-year due to robust customer demand, higher jewellery sales, and strengthening brand recall.
evidence.quote: Revenue increased by ~60% year-on-year, driven by robust customer demand, higher jewellery sales, and strengthening brand recall.

evidence.fact: RBZ Jewellers plans to launch its Surat store in Quarter 2 and Rajkot, Maninagar, and Gandhinagar stores in Quarter 3.
evidence.quote: So, Surat will be launching in Quarter 2 and Rajkot in early Quarter 3. And same, I think Maninagar and Gandhinagar both will be launched in Quarter 3 itself.

evidence.fact: The capital expenditure incurred for the Surat store is approximately INR 10 crores.
evidence.quote: Approximately INR10 crores is the capex incurred for Surat store.

evidence.fact: Large format stores feature around 10,000 square feet carpet area while mid-format stores are around 5,000 square feet.
evidence.quote: The large format stores are typically around 10,000 square feet carpet area and mid format stores are 5,000 square feet carpet area.

evidence.fact: EBITDA for Q1 FY27 reached INR 18 crores with an EBITDA margin of 14.9%.
evidence.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is INR18 crores reflecting a healthy growth of 39% Y-o-Y, with EBITDA margins coming in a healthy 14.9%.

evidence.fact: Stagnant average gold rates resulted in negligible inventory gain during Quarter 1.
evidence.quote: One is that the average gold rate has remained stagnant and thus there is negligible inventory gain in the system as of now.

evidence.fact: Quarterly margins were affected by lease asset amortization of INR 76 lakhs and lease liabilities impact of INR 115 lakhs.
evidence.quote: The amortization of lease assets is INR76 lakhs and the impact of lease liabilities is at INR115 lakhs.

evidence.fact: The company's factory capacity stands at 1.8 to 2 tons per year and is currently operating at around 50% utilization.
evidence.quote: The total capacity still remains at around 1.8 to 2 tons a year. And the production that we are doing or the consumption that we are able to do is somewhere around 900 kgs to 1000 kgs. So, we are utilizing factory at around 50% of capacity.

evidence.fact: During peak season periods, factory capacity utilization ranges from 70% to 90%.
evidence.quote: In the season times, currently as of now, our capacity utilization generally goes at 70%, 80% minimum, 75%, 85% sometimes, depending on which days are all, sometimes it is near to 90% or so.

evidence.fact: Job work services accounted for 52% of the total gold volumes sold in FY26.
evidence.quote: Accounted for 52% of total gold volumes sold in FY26, highlighting its strategic importance to the business.

evidence.fact: RBZ Jewellers has sanctioned debt facilities of around INR 300 crores.
evidence.quote: Given that we have a sanctioned debt of around INR300 crores.

evidence.fact: Sanctioned debt limits remain unutilized and are sufficient to fund the four upcoming store expansions in this financial year.
evidence.quote: And we are yet to utilize it, which is sufficient for the four stores that is coming in this financial year.

evidence.fact: The company plans to progressively transition its inventory financing towards Gold Metal Loans to keep inventory hedged.
evidence.quote: GML we are planning that during the course of the journey we should actually have an inventory which is hedged.

evidence.fact: Carrying inventory in an unhedged open position poses commodity price risks to ongoing business operations.
evidence.quote: Now what you talk about the inventory levels, it is a directional call that we have taken that on an ongoing business if we were to, put our inventory and this amount of inventory onto, let's say in an open position, it is going to call for risk.

evidence.fact: The company notes that recent restrictions on gold imports are not advantageous.
evidence.quote: Certainly, I think these restrictions are not advantageous, but up to what level there is an impact is crucial.

evidence.fact: The industry sentiment and buying remain low in late quarter 1 post Akshay Tritiya.
evidence.quote: Now when you talk about the industry quarter 1 post Akshay Tritiya remains low in terms of sentiments and all in the buying -- there is no buying season as such in late quarter 1.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): RBZ Jewellers will launch its Surat store in Quarter 2 and its Rajkot, Maninagar, and Gandhinagar stores in Quarter 3.
evidence.quote: So, Surat will be launching in Quarter 2 and Rajkot in early Quarter 3. And same, I think Maninagar and Gandhinagar both will be launched in Quarter 3 itself.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The company expects 18-karat jewellery to make up at least 20% of its corporate sales mix by the end of this year.
evidence.quote: So we have introduced this since December, our sales mix in corporate, before it was 100% 22 carat, I see by the end of this year, it will be at least 20% will be of 18 caratage.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): Management targets store capex break-even to be achieved within a year or less.
evidence.quote: The capex when you say about the break-even point, the capex break-even will be achieved in a year or less.
